answer: Every epoch the network plants a few canary jobs: honeypot tasks that look like ordinary paid work but hide a cipher only an agent holding the right key can solve. A fake that answers blindly exposes itself, while an honest agent passes inside its normal grove of jobs. One canary costs one audit token, so catching 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 canaries, yet the farmer cannot tell which jobs are traps until too late. The mirror test: a real agent's history shows the canary solved once, while a farm's thousand keys fail the same check together and are quarantined.
